claim: A leniently parsed signed payload splits honest consumers: two mainstream readers of the same signed bytes obtain different documents.

environment.what: python in-toto 3.1.0 over securesystemslib 1.4.0, plus whatever JSON parsers the host has
assumptions: the signer is the adversary: an attacker cannot add a duplicate member without re-signing

counterexample.means: the split does NOT reproduce: every available parser reads the duplicate member last-wins. If this ever exits 0, a parser has started disagreeing and this entry must be re-litigated

negative_control.means: a strict I-JSON reader refuses the same bytes, so the leniency is a choice rather than a necessity

applies_until: A consumer parser that takes first-wins or refuses duplicates is shown in a real deployment, or the library adopts a strict reader at the signed boundary.

cost.to_discover: one afternoon: install, three probes, and a five-parser measurement
cost.to_recheck: seconds — the witness measures the parsers present
